A: Panel A is a dermoscopic image of actinic cheilitis showing the captioned structureless areas; this feature is not in the allowed vocabulary, so it is proposed. B: Panel B is a dermoscopic image of actinic cheilitis with scales, matching the scaling finding in the allowed vocabulary. C: Panel C is a dermoscopic image of actinic cheilitis showing the captioned white halo of the vermilion border, which is not represented by an allowed finding key. D: Panel D is a dermoscopic image of actinic cheilitis showing telangiectatic and tortuous vessels as stated in the caption; this dermoscopic vessel feature is proposed because it is absent from the allowed vocabulary.

panels.figure_caption: Dermoscopic features of AC: (A) Structureless areas; (B) Scales; (C) White halo of the vermilion border; (D) Telangiectatic and torturous blood vessels.
in_text_mentions: White structureless areas (Figure 2A), scales (Figure 2B), and white halo of the vermilion border (Figure 2C) are described frequently (11, 12). The blood vessels are telangiectatic and tortuous (Figure 2D), but sometimes polymorphous vessels can be seen (2). Island-like structures with white projections and vascular telangiectasia disposed radially to an ulcerated area were described by Ito et al. (11). The ulcerated lesion is covered by a crust described by dermatoscopy as a brown structureless area.

in_text_mentions: The prevalence of AC was 12% in the sample studied. Among the 36 cases of AC, 30 participants (83.4%) had chronic AC and 6 (16.6%) had acute AC. All cases were identified in the region of the lower lip. Regarding the severity of AC, all acute cases were classified as mild. Among the cases of chronic AC, 20 (66.6%) were mild, nine (30.0%) were moderate, and only one case (3.3%) was severe. The most common clinical findings in chronic AC lesions are illustrated in figure 2 . Only 13 (4.33%) rural workers reported being aware of AC, particularly its etiology.

plate_findings.evidence: Diffuse white plaque, accompanied by a venous lake on the right side of the lower lip
Painful ulceration associated with whitish plaques

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Clinical photograph of a patient's lower lip in an article on monitoring actinic cheilitis; caption describes a diffuse white plaque (leukoplakia) of the lower lip, a recognized manifestation of actinic cheilitis, with visible vermilion atrophy and a coexisting venous lake. B: Clinical photograph of a patient's lower lip from the actinic cheilitis cohort; caption documents painful ulceration with whitish plaques on the lower lip vermilion, consistent with ulcerated/keratotic actinic cheilitis. C: Clinical photograph of the lower lip of an evaluated patient; caption describes whitish plaques with erosive areas, manifestations of actinic cheilitis in a study dedicated to this disease. D: Clinical photograph of the lower lip of an evaluated patient; caption documents whitish plaques with erosive areas, consistent with actinic cheilitis in a disease-focused study.

in_text_mentions: disagreement was found in only one patient—at the remote consultation, pigmentation and erosion were presented, while none of these findings could be encountered at in‐person consultation, but the presence of plaques. Table 2 summarizes the percentage agreement between consultations. Considering that face‐to‐face consultation remains the gold standard for clinical evaluation, and acknowledging that photographic assessment may be subject to some degree of discrepancy, no clinical intervention was undertaken in this case. Representative photos of the evaluated cases may be observed in Figure 1.

plate_findings.evidence: a case of actinic cheilitis that presented mild dysplasia

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E histology of a confirmed actinic cheilitis case showing mild epithelial dysplasia and intense solar elastosis, both vocabulary-supported histologic manifestations of actinic cheilitis. B: Immunohistochemistry of the same actinic cheilitis case demonstrating PD-L1 expression in dysplastic basal cells; disease attribution from panel-specific caption and article title. C: Immunohistochemistry showing mild CD4+ cell infiltration in the lamina propria of an actinic cheilitis case; specific immunophenotype not present in the vocabulary. D: Immunohistochemistry showing mild CD8+ cell infiltration in the lamina propria of an actinic cheilitis case; specific immunophenotype not present in the vocabulary.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A is an immunohistochemical image of actinic cheilitis without epithelial dysplasia, showing low-grade 8-OHdG nuclear immunoreactivity; it is a real patient tissue image of the target disease but lacks a vocabulary-listed finding. B: Panel B shows actinic cheilitis with mild epithelial dysplasia on immunohistochemistry for 8-OHdG, supporting the target disease with a captioned histologic manifestation. C: Panel C shows actinic cheilitis with moderate epithelial dysplasia and strong nuclear 8-OHdG immunostaining, directly supporting the target disease. D: Panel D shows actinic cheilitis with moderate epithelial dysplasia and predominantly cytoplasmic 8-OHdG staining, a less common staining pattern described in the article.
